To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the related words which are extracted from the document set are more useful as an addition to the current keywords than related words which have been extracted from the document collection and (b) the related words extracted with non-taxonomical relation are more effective for increasing human-computer interaction.

the addition of words with taxonomical relations to the current query is useful in information retrieval, and that the addition of non-taxonomical related words is also useful, especially in cases of queries that are not very precise.

the inclusion of words with a taxonomical relation to the current keyword is more effective than the addition of words with a non-taxonomical relation, and that the addition of a word with a taxonomically close relation is more effective than that of a word with an intermediate taxonomical relation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: 1) How to extract a word set from documents for human-computer interaction in information retrieval. 2) What kind of word is more useful as a retrieval support word for human-computer interactions.
how we can make human-computing interaction more creative and effective.
how human-computer interaction is improved by adding related words which have been extracted from documents to the current query.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of taxonomical words is better than that of non-taxonomical words in terms of retrieval performance and user satisfaction.
the use of non-taxonomical related words as additional keywords is more useful for human-computer interaction than the use of taxonomical related words.

the words with a high degree of inclusion in the query are useful for retrieval support, and the words which have a high degree of exclusion in the query are also useful for retrieval support in the case of the query being too narrow.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can extract word sets from documents and use them as a retrieval support tool.
the words with taxonomical relations are more useful than words with non-taxonomical ones, but the words with non-taxonomy are more effective than the words with no relations.
the word set extracted with taxonomical relation is more useful for human-computer interaction in the course of retrieval support.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of words with a taxonomical relation to the query is more effective than that of words with a non-taxonomical relation.
the use of case-marking particles is effective for the purpose of increasing human-computer interaction.
the use of non-taxonomical related words is more effective for retrieval than taxonomical ones.
